checks.scope: Literal theorem and reduction to a single 68-member family

checks.method: Inspected GLOBAL67-dependency-roadmap.md sections 1 and 2 and PRIOR_DELTA18_UNLOCK.md against manuscript sections 3 through 6.
checks.observation: The architectural chain covers degrees 20, 19, 18, 17, 16 and at most 15 after the universal cap20. Cross-star, crowding, minimum7 and R61 are activated only after degree19 is excluded, when cap18 and mu41 both hold. D16 and cap15 are framed as conditional case theorems until their degree guards are established. This checks the declared dependency design, not all source-code dependencies.
checks.scope: Global maximum-degree coverage and import activation

checks.method: Read D17-complete-argument.md sections Statement and direct scope, Root-link alternatives, P9 finite projections, and Exact arithmetic and its scope.
checks.observation: The projection uses each actual complete root link. Every proper exact trace counts all exterior completions, including the empty trace; only full four-point traces are binary. An E3 marker represents its actual exterior point without bounding other exterior support. The document separately lists versioned mathematical bridges and distinguishes shared-producer coefficient replay from literal orbit/ancestry checking. This supports the manuscript framing but does not independently validate every row.
checks.scope: High-degree finite projection versus arbitrary ambient support

checks.method: Followed R15-rho6-completed-evidence.md to R15-degree2-independent-ordinary-check.md; inspected its normalization, whole-completion exterior budget and eleven-point moment argument, and compared manuscript section 5.2.
checks.observation: The support argument first treats degree2 through 91 and 78 normalized motifs. Its new-point budget bounds the entire six-triple completion by three new points, rather than assigning three fresh points separately per triple. With minimum degree3, the displayed incidence identity yields 60 <= 285/2 - 7n and hence integer n <= 11; the maximum-degree-at-most4 alternative yields 225/4 < 60. Thus padding to eleven labels is stated only after a universal support reduction. I did not rerun the motif checker or proof trees in this round.
checks.scope: New fifteen-triple contribution and finite-domain justification

checks.method: Compared manuscript sections 2 and 7 with EXTERNAL-H27-JIN-SCOPE.md and GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md.
checks.observation: H27 is identified as an imported computer-assisted preprint theorem without local full-ledger replay; Jin is attributed through Nikiforov Theorem A with original full-text access limitation. The manuscript states that Lean covers selected lemmas and arithmetic interfaces, not the complete extremal theorem. These are appropriate methodological qualifications; this check did not independently retrieve or re-prove the external theorems.

findings.disposition: Manuscript sections 3.1 and 7 and D17-complete-argument.md explicitly disclose this dependence and assign the geometric implication to separate versioned bridges. Preserve this distinction during later evidence review.
findings.statement: The exact coefficient replay retains shared model construction, so its correctness assurance does not by itself establish the family-to-model map or every mathematical strengthening row.

findings.disposition: The manuscript correctly keeps unrestricted exterior multiplicities in proper traces, while the size-15 route proves a whole-completion exterior budget and then an eleven-point support bound before enumeration. Later rounds should test those bridge obligations and their exact domain implementations.
findings.statement: Arbitrary-support completeness is supported by distinct mechanisms in the high-degree projections and the size-15 search, and should not be collapsed into a single finite-support claim.

content.summary: The contract, definitions and contribution are coherently framed as an ordinary computer-assisted exclusion of exactly 68 members on arbitrary support. The manuscript separates theorem imports, written family-to-model implications, shared-builder arithmetic replay and independently implemented coverage. The degree-case dependency order is explicit and exhaustive at the architectural level. This Round 1 inspection found no necessary framing revision; it does not certify every finite leaf or imported theorem proof.
